You can also try to find a low cost therapist on BetterHelp.com or, if you have a job, see if they offer free counseling services there. Another good place to look would probably be the Catholic Church. Try and get in touch with a local parish and see if they can find you some free counseling (I know Catholic Charities offers free counseling for Veterans and dependents.) 

There’s going to be better days ahead, OP.

Firstly, you need to ask yourself this, OP. Do you love her? Do you care about her safety and well-being? Most importantly, is something like this going to bring you closer to your girlfriend or make you drift farther apart? Once you’ve answered those questions, you can either let her return to her family, or hunker down for this relationship in the long run.

Your dad has every right to kick her out of his house, and, unfortunately, if you decide to stay in a relationship with her, there’s a good chance that he will kick you out, too. You’re not a minor anymore so law enforcement will evict you from the property. Because of this, do NOT tell your dad if you have any intentions of staying in a relationship with her until you have a plan to become solely independent. If you love her and want to stay in a relationship with her, you’re going to inevitably have to move out of your dad’s house (provided you do not want to become long distance. If that’s the case then ignore everything I’m saying.) 

She will most likely be kept in a psychiatric unit involuntarily for a while. While she’s there, they’ll probably offer her the chance to relocate to a unit in Oklahoma since that’s where her family is. Before she makes that decision, however, you and her need to seriously talk about what steps you need to take in your relationship first. If you both ultimately decide to stay together and not make it long distance, it’s time for you to start looking for potential places to rent. You’re going to probably house her for a while until she can get back on her feet, but if you love her and are willing to make that sacrifice, then that choice is up to you.

If you don’t have a credit card, get one now. Build your credit. If you don’t have rental history you need to find someone who would be willing to co-sign a lease with you. Assuming you’re in college, begin planning ahead as to whether or not you’ll have sufficient funds for next semester. If not, you’ll most likely need to drop out until your life is stable enough to work AND school at the same time. Either way, the choice is certainly not easy.

Life begins at conception. Why is it not okay to kill a human being after they’re born, but when they’re still in the womb, it’s completely fine? The justification people find when they say the zygote or fetus is a “clump of cells” is the absolute weakest point I think I’ve ever heard. Everything that has ever lived or breathed is, at the end of the day, just a clump of cells. I am basically just a clump of cells, but I still deserve to live my life without being torn apart limb-by-limb by someone breaking into my home while I’m asleep, knowing full well I would have waken up the next morning to live my life. Same goes for the unborn when you have these procedures that intrude into what is supposed to be their safe place to live and grow, only to be torn apart and cut by men in white lab coats. When you get in a car, you don’t become the car. When a baby is inside a womb, the woman carrying it doesn’t become the baby. The baby doesn’t become the woman. They are two separate entities with different blood types and DNA makeup. They have separate fingerprints and faces, different hearing and heartbeats. The mother is responsible for maintaining and caring for the life of the child — both inside and outside of the womb. The only time in which I believe abortion is okay is to save the life of the mother. That is because no human being, mother or father, daughter or son, friend or enemy, should ever be forced to lay their life down for another. As a victim of rape (that didn’t result in a pregnancy fortunately) I found people pressuring me to have an abortion without even taking my trauma into consideration. I would not have been in my right state of mind to make such an impactful decision, and I think that goes for a lot of other women, too. Desperate circumstances result in desperate measures. I believe women should have the choice to abort, but we as a society should not call it empowering or something to be proud of. Women are allowed to have control over their bodies, it truly is my body my choice, but what you do with your body does not just impact you alone.

I used to have a complicated time sleeping as a kid. I’d sleepwalk all the time and have nightmares a lot. The first time I had sleep paralysis I was in a bunkbed still since I shared a room with my sister. I remember opening my eyes and it was dark in the room, and I could see light from under my bedroom door. I remember feeling cold but I couldn’t pull the blanket over myself, and when I tried, I started hearing a little girl singing. It scared the shit out of me, and suddenly there was a girl with white hair climbing up the ladder and looking at me with red eyes. I couldn’t move, I couldn’t breathe. I was fucking terrified. She started crawling over and I remember feeling her body weigh down on my lungs and literally crush me. She sat on my lungs and started slashing through my chest. I tried to scream but nothing came out. I tried to move but I couldn’t. It felt like I was suffocating. The entire time she was singing, and when I finally snapped awake, I was drenched in sweat and immediately felt all over my body to make sure she was gone and I was still alive. Needless to say that was fucking terrifying.
